title: Authentication and Authorization in Web Applications
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of authentication and authorization in web applications in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply authentication and authorization in web applications in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to managing sensitive operations and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Authentication and Authorization in Web Applications through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding authentication and authorization in web applications helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Authentication and Authorization in Web Applications helps you reason about identity verification. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Identity verification. Then connect it to Roles and permissions. The remaining syllabus points—Access checks at appropriate boundaries, Managing sensitive operations—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Authentication and Authorization in Web Applications

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports authentication and authorization in web applications. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain authentication and authorization in web applications, identify its place in ruby web development and apis, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
